summary.text: Ann Seeley is standing for Family First in Kew at the 2026 Victorian election, her second run for the party in this seat after 2022, when she polled 1.7 per cent. She was also the party's candidate for the federal seat of Menzies in 2025. Her party says she was one of the founding delegates of Family First and worked with Steve Fielding from the outset. Her background includes 13 years with Channel 10 News and five years running the Kew Baptist Youth Hostel as its live-in manager.

prior_roles.note: Her party page mentions her earnings as a real estate agent in the past tense but does not say whether she still works as one.

summary.text: David Laird is One Nation's candidate for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC describes him as an institutional banker who has worked at ANZ and the Commonwealth Bank and has been managing director of a capital advisory firm. It adds that he has a master's degree in e-commerce from Deakin University, where he has lectured to MBA and MPA students. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Kew: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: David Sun is Labor's candidate for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election. His party presents him as a father bringing up his children in the area, and says he supports Labor's plans for health care and schools there. Neither Labor nor the ABC had published any further biography, such as his work or past roles, as at early November 2026.

priorities.text: Better local health care and schools in Kew, in line with Labor's plans

summary.text: Finlay Davis, a lawyer who says he has lived in Kew for most of his life, is standing as an independent for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election. His campaign site says he graduated in law from Monash University in 1974, has practised for close to 50 years, including a spell as a commercial and tax lawyer in the Cook Islands and Hong Kong, and founded two sports businesses, the ticketing firm Corporate Sports Unlimited and Corporate Sports Travel. An independent of the same name also contested Kew in 2022.

prior_roles.role: Founder and director, Corporate Sports Travel Pty Ltd
Founder and director, Corporate Sports Unlimited (sports ticketing)
Commercial and tax lawyer in the Cook Islands and Hong Kong

previous_candidacies.note: Matched by name, seat and independent status; his campaign site doesn't mention the 2022 race.

A royal commission into the planning and contract costs of the Big Build
Pegging MPs' base salary to average earnings and limiting them to three terms
About 2,000 extra police, with better pay and longer training
A national housing plan built around growth in regional cities

summary.text: Jackie Carter is the Greens candidate for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election, having also stood for the party in this seat in 2022, when she won 8.3 per cent of the primary vote. At the 2025 federal election she was the Greens candidate for Kooyong and received about 7.8 per cent. Born in Kew, she says she has spent more than 20 years in information technology roles in the pharmaceutical industry.

occupation.text: IT professional in the pharmaceutical sector

priorities.text: Action on the climate emergency
Tackling the housing and cost-of-living crises and widening wealth inequality
Restoring public services and trust in politics
It's time to vote for someone who can't be bought.

summary.text: Jess Wilson has represented Kew for the Liberal Party since winning the seat in 2022. In November 2025 she became Leader of the Opposition, the first woman to hold the Victorian Liberal leadership, and she also holds the shadow treasury portfolio. Before entering Parliament she was a senior policy executive with the Business Council of Australia. She is standing again in Kew in 2026.

occupation.text: Lawyer; policy executive at the Business Council of Australia

prior_roles.role: Leader of the Opposition and Leader of the Victorian Liberal Party
Shadow Minister for Education; Shadow Minister for Industry and Economic Growth
Shadow Minister for Early Childhood and Education
Shadow Minister for Finance; Shadow Minister for Economic Reform and Regulation
Shadow Minister for Home Ownership and Housing Affordability
Adviser to federal Treasurer Josh Frydenberg

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia places her presidency in 2016 without giving start or end dates.

faction.name: Liberal moderate
faction.note: Wikipedia says she is widely seen as a moderate within the party.

summary.text: Samantha Lincolne, known as Sam, is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election. On her party page she says she has organised through her student union and in her workplace, on issues such as free education, public housing and opposition to racism. She frames her run as a challenge to capitalism and to politicians she sees as cut off from working people.

priorities.text: I am running to challenge the entire system of capitalism
Easing cost-of-living pressure and the housing crisis, which she blames on governments favouring landlords and developers
Opposing cuts to public sector jobs and further privatisation
Free education and more public housing

summary.text: Sophie Torney is an independent candidate for Kew at the 2026 Victorian election and a councillor for Studley Ward on Boroondara City Council, where she was mayor from 2024 to 2025. She first contested Kew in 2022, finishing third with 21.1 per cent of the primary vote. A former software programmer and project manager who later started and ran businesses, she became a board member of the Accountability Round Table, an integrity advocacy group, in 2023 and was made its chair in 2025.

prior_roles.note: Her About page says she joined the board in 2023 and was appointed chair in 2025; her policy page calls her the former chair. No end year is given.

priorities.text: Stronger anti-corruption laws, including a broader definition of corruption and wider powers for IBAC
Fiscal rules for government, such as an operating surplus and a falling ratio of net debt to state output
Giving councils and their communities more say over planning while meeting state housing targets
Protecting native forests and parks, and ending duck hunting
I support Treaty in Victoria.
